I think that we usually just omit name components that are not present instead of using placeholders like `unknown`.
Noticed that spec https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/registry/attributes/db/#db-client-connection-pool-name provides some guidance on how to create a name when it is not available. Idk whether this is a viable strategy since these properties might not be available either.

So the idea here is that when there are multiple data sources with the same name we'll append a suffix. Since we are not doing this for other connection pool instrumentations it is questionable whether we should be doing this here. If we decide to do this then we should apply the same strategy across the connection pool instrumentations.
cc @trask any suggestions on how to handle this?

Pending the discussion in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/19160#discussion_r3564889077, I think we should avoid process-local `-N` suffixes here. If no stable name exists, use a stable fallback and let duplicates merge so metric identities remain consistent across restarts.

[General] This fallback is unreachable for a `DbInfo` returned by `JdbcConnectionUrlParser.parse(...)`. The only two places that set the legacy `dbName` override (`MssqlUrlParser` and `JtdsUrlParser`, for named instances) also set `namespace` on the same path, so `getDbNamespace()` is always populated whenever `getDbName()` is. Your #19160 and #19173 versions of this method already just read `getDbNamespace()`.

```suggestion
    String dbNamespace = dbInfo.getDbNamespace();
```

`compileOnly` makes `JdbcConnectionUrlParser` available only while compiling, while `testInstrumentation` masks the missing runtime dependency in tests. A custom agent distribution that includes Druid but not JDBC will therefore hit `NoClassDefFoundError` in `getDataSourceName`; the advice suppresses it and emits no pool metrics. Declare the JDBC javaagent as an actual module dependency, as other cross-instrumentation dependencies do (for example, `instrumentation/servlet/servlet-3.0/javaagent/build.gradle.kts:19`).

This same block now exists in four PRs (#19108, #19159, #19160, #19173) and the copies have already drifted apart. Since they're landing together it would be good if they were literally identical, which makes the later cleanup trivial.

Since #19366 landed, `ParseContext.host()` strips the brackets off literal IPv6 addresses, so `DbInfo.getServerAddress()` always holds the bare address - the extra `startsWith("[")` check can never fire. Dropping it also matches apache-dbcp2 (#19160) and tomcat-jdbc (#19173), which don't have it.

```suggestion
      if (serverAddress.indexOf(':') >= 0) {
```

I opened #19370 to fold the four copies into one shared helper after these land.
I don't think we want the `-N` suffix, similar to discussions on the other PRs.
